title: Blueberries and Cardiovascular Health: Findings from a 12-Week Clinical Trial
metaDescription: We analyze a 12-week clinical trial on the impact of blueberries on the cardiometabolic health of adults with elevated blood pressure.
excerpt: A controlled study evaluated the effect of daily wild blueberry consumption in older adults with elevated blood pressure. We analyze what the data revealed.
imageAlt: Bowl with fresh wild blueberries on a light wooden table

blocks.text: Introduction: Research on Blueberries and Vascular Health

The relationship between nutrition and cardiovascular well-being has received considerable scientific attention in recent years. Within the small fruit category, wild blueberries have stood out in various analyses due to their profile of bioactive compounds and polyphenols. However, evaluating their actual impact on endothelial function and specific hemodynamic parameters requires well-designed and rigorous clinical trials.

Understanding how the bodies of middle-aged and older adults with above-normal blood pressure respond is fundamental to determining whether certain dietary habits produce significant changes in the circulatory system. Below, we examine the results of a recent clinical study aimed at answering this question.
What the Source Says: Details and Results of the Clinical Trial

The study published in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm clinical trial. The researchers included 52 participants (postmenopausal women and men) aged between 40 and 75 years who presented with elevated blood pressure or stage 1 hypertension.

Over a 12-week period, one group consumed 22 grams of freeze-dried wild blueberry powder daily, while the control group received an isocaloric placebo. The primary objective was to evaluate endothelial function through the reactive hyperemia index (RHI). Secondary objectives examined arterial stiffness, brachial and aortic hemodynamics, various blood cardiometabolic biomarkers, and the composition of the gut microbiota.

items: Endothelial function: Wild blueberry consumption did not produce a significant improvement in endothelial function or in most cardiometabolic parameters compared to placebo (P > 0.05).

Aortic pulse pressure: A treatment-by-time interaction was observed in aortic pulse pressure, which increased in the blueberry group compared to placebo (+3.0 mmHg; 95% CI: 0.29 to 5.67; P = 0.03). The researchers highlighted that this was an isolated finding that was not accompanied by unfavorable changes in other hemodynamic parameters or arterial stiffness.
Changes in the placebo group: Some hemodynamic changes were recorded within the placebo group that did not occur in the group consuming blueberries.

Gut microbiota: No significant differences were observed in alpha or beta diversity of the microbiota between both groups over time, although the overall composition of microbial communities showed modest variations.

blocks.text: Additionally, exploratory analyses of the study indicated that participants' baseline microbial richness was associated with improvements in endothelial function, particularly within the group that consumed wild blueberries. Limitations of the work include the relatively small sample size (52 participants) and the specificity of the group evaluated.
Context: Individual Variability and Precision Nutrition

The findings of this trial add valuable nuances to the existing body of literature. Although previous research suggested potential vascular benefits of blueberries, the results of controlled trials can be divergent. This study underscores that the effects of a food are not always uniform across all populations or baseline health conditions.
The researchers noted that an individual's baseline gut microbiota may contribute to response variability, highlighting the need for larger studies with precision nutrition approaches.
The interaction between gut bacterial composition and dietary phytochemicals helps explain why different individuals may experience distinct physiological responses when consuming the same foods.
What It Means for You: Practical Application in Daily Routine
For the general public and those seeking to improve their diet, the results of this type of research offer a balanced perspective:

items: Wholesome diet: Blueberries are a nutritious fruit that can be part of a varied eating pattern, without attributing miraculous properties to them or expecting them to resolve complex conditions such as elevated blood pressure on their own.
Comprehensive health approach: Managing cardiovascular health requires a set of sustainable habits including physical activity, adequate rest, and following corresponding medical recommendations.
Individual responses: Each organism processes nutrients in a unique way, so a diverse diet that includes fruits, vegetables, and whole grains remains the most recommended strategy.

blocks.text: The 12-week clinical trial demonstrated that daily supplementation with 22 grams of freeze-dried wild blueberries did not produce direct improvements in endothelial function in adults with elevated blood pressure, suggesting that individual factors such as the gut microbiota influence bodily absorption and response.
